sanskrit: śunaḥśepaṃ naraśreṣṭha gṛhītvā tu mahāyaśāḥ vyaśrāmyat puṣkare rājā madhyāhne raghunandana
english: Having taken Śunaḥśepa, O best of men, that greatly renowned king rested at Puṣkara at midday, O joy of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: tasya viśramamāṇasya śunaḥśepo mahāyaśāḥ puṣkaraṃ śreṣṭham āgamya viśvāmitraṃ dadarśa ha
english: While he was resting, the greatly renowned Śunaḥśepa came to the foremost of holy places, Puṣkara, and beheld Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇavadano dīnas tṛṣṇayā ca śrameṇa ca papātāṅke mune rāma vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: With a dejected face, wretched with thirst and exhaustion, he fell upon the sage's lap, O Rāma, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: na me 'sti mātā na pitā jñātayo bāndhavāḥ kutaḥ trātum arhasi māṃ saumya dharmeṇa munipuṃgava
english: I have no mother, no father — where then are kinsmen or relatives? O gentle one, O bull among sages, you ought to protect me through righteousness.

sanskrit: trātā tvaṃ hi muniśreṣṭha sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ hi bhāvanaḥ rājā ca kṛtakāryaḥ syād ahaṃ dīrghāyur avyayaḥ
english: For you are the protector of all, O best of sages; you are the sustainer of all. The king would have his purpose fulfilled, and I would live long and imperishably.

sanskrit: svargalokam upāśnīyāṃ tapas taptvā hy anuttamam sa me nātho hy anāthasya bhava bhavyena cetasā piteva putraṃ dharmātmaṃs trātum arhasi kilbiṣāt
english: I would attain the heavenly world, having practised the highest austerity. Be my protector, for I am without a protector — with a gracious heart, O soul of righteousness, you ought to rescue me from sin as a father rescues a son.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ sāntvayitvā bahuvidhaṃ putrān idam uvāca ha
english: Having heard those words of his, the great ascetic Viśvāmitra consoled him in many ways and then spoke these words to his sons.

sanskrit: yatkṛte pitaraḥ putrāñ janayanti śubhārthinaḥ paralokahitārthāya tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: The time has now come for that purpose for which fathers who seek the good beget sons — for the benefit of the next world.

sanskrit: ayaṃ munisuto bālo mattaḥ śaraṇam icchati asya jīvitamātreṇa priyaṃ kuruta putrakāḥ
english: This young son of a sage seeks shelter from me; do something dear for him at the mere cost of your own life, my sons.

sanskrit: sarve sukṛtakarmāṇaḥ sarve dharmaparāyaṇāḥ paśubhūtā narendrasya tṛptim agneḥ prayacchata
english: All of you are doers of good deeds, all of you are devoted to righteousness — become the sacrificial animal of the king and grant satisfaction to the fire.

sanskrit: nāthavāṃś ca śunaḥśepo yajñaś cāvighnato bhavet devatās tarpitāś ca syur mama cāpi kṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Śunaḥśepa would have a protector, the sacrifice would proceed without hindrance, the gods would be satisfied, and my word too would be fulfilled.

sanskrit: munes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā madhuṣyandādayaḥ sutāḥ sābhimānaṃ naraśreṣṭha salīlam idam abruvan
english: Hearing the sage's words, O best of men, his sons — Madhuṣyanda and the others — spoke these words with arrogance and disdain.

sanskrit: katham ātmasutān hitvā trāyase 'nyasutaṃ vibho akāryam iva paśyāmaḥ śvamāṃsam iva bhojane
english: How, O lord, do you abandon your own sons to rescue another's son? We regard this as improper, like eating dog-flesh at a meal.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā putrāṇāṃ munipuṃgavaḥ krodhasaṃraktanayano vyāhartum upacakrame
english: Hearing those words of his sons, the bull among sages, with eyes reddened by anger, began to speak.

sanskrit: niḥsādhvasam idaṃ proktaṃ dharmād api vigarhitam atikramya tu madvākyaṃ dāruṇaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: This speech was uttered shamelessly, censured even by the law of righteousness — cruel and hair-raising, it transgresses my command.

sanskrit: śvamāṃsabhojinaḥ sarve vāsiṣṭhā iva jātiṣu pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu pṛthivyām anuvatsyatha
english: All of you shall wander the earth for a full thousand years in your clans as eaters of dog-flesh, like the Vasiṣṭhas.

sanskrit: kṛtvā śāpasamāyuktān putrān munivaras tadā śunaḥśepam uvācārtaṃ kṛtvā rakṣāṃ nirāmayām
english: Having thus afflicted his sons with the curse, that best of sages then spoke to the distressed Śunaḥśepa, granting him a wholesome protection.

sanskrit: pavitrapāśair āsakto raktamālyānulepanaḥ vaiṣṇavaṃ yūpam āsādya vāgbhir agnim udāhara
english: Bound with sacred cords, adorned with red garlands and unguents, approach the sacrificial post of Viṣṇu and invoke the fire with these hymns.

sanskrit: ime tu gāthe dve divye gāyethā muniputraka ambarīṣasya yajñe 'smiṃs tataḥ siddhim avāpsyasi
english: Chant these two divine hymns, O son of a sage, at this sacrifice of Ambarīṣa — thereby you shall attain fulfilment.

sanskrit: śunaḥśepo gṛhītvā te dve gāthe susamāhitaḥ tvarayā rājasiṃhaṃ tam ambarīṣam uvāca ha
english: Śunaḥśepa, having received those two hymns with concentrated mind, quickly spoke to Ambarīṣa, that lion among kings.

sanskrit: rājasiṃha mahāsattva śīghraṃ gacchāvahe sadaḥ nivartayasva rājendra dīkṣāṃ ca samupāhara
english: O lion among kings, O great-spirited one, let us go quickly to the assembly hall; resume the rite, O lord of kings, and bring forward the consecration.

sanskrit: tad vākyam ṛṣiputrasya śrutvā harṣaṃ samutsukaḥ jagāma nṛpatiḥ śīghraṃ yajñavāṭam atandritaḥ
english: Hearing those words of the sage's son, the king, filled with eager joy, went swiftly and without delay to the sacrificial enclosure.

sanskrit: sadasyānumate rājā pavitrakṛtalakṣaṇam paśuṃ raktāmbaraṃ kṛtvā yūpe taṃ samabandhayat
english: With the assent of the officiants, the king dressed Śunaḥśepa with sacred marks and a red garment and bound him to the sacrificial post.

sanskrit: sa baddho vāgbhir agryābhir abhituṣṭāva vai surau indram indrānujaṃ caiva yathāvan muniputrakaḥ
english: Bound to the post, that son of a sage duly propitiated the two gods — Indra and the younger brother of Indra — with the foremost hymns.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītaḥ sahasrākṣo rahasyastutitarpitaḥ dīrgham āyus tadā prādāc chunaḥśepāya rāghava
english: Then Sahasrākṣa (Indra), pleased and satisfied by the esoteric hymns of praise, granted long life to Śunaḥśepa, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: sa ca rājā naraśreṣṭha yajñasya ca samāptavān phalaṃ bahuguṇaṃ rāma sahasrākṣaprasādajam
english: And that king, O best of men, O Rāma, obtained the manifold fruit of the sacrifice, born of the grace of Sahasrākṣa.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi dharmātmā bhūyas tepe mahātapāḥ puṣkareṣu naraśreṣṭha daśavarṣaśatāni ca
english: And Viśvāmitra, the righteous-souled one of great austerity, practised severe penance once more at Puṣkara for a full thousand years, O best of men.

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu vratasnātaṃ mahāmunim abhyāgacchan surāḥ sarve tapaḥphalacikīrṣavaḥ
english: When the thousand years were complete, all the gods came to the great sage who had bathed upon completion of his vow, wishing to bestow the fruit of his austerity.

sanskrit: abravīt sumahātejā brahmā suruciraṃ vacaḥ ṛṣis tvam asi bhadraṃ te svārjitaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: Brahmā of great splendour spoke pleasant words: 'You are a ṛṣi — good fortune to you — by the meritorious deeds you yourself have earned.'

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā deveśas tridivaṃ punar abhyagāt viśvāmitro mahātejā bhūyas tepe mahat tapaḥ
english: Having thus spoken to him, the lord of gods departed once more to the three heavens; Viśvāmitra of great splendour then practised great austerity again.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena mahatā menakā paramāpsarāḥ puṣkareṣu naraśreṣṭha snātuṃ samupacakrame
english: Then after a great length of time, Menakā, the foremost among the apsarases, O best of men, came to Puṣkara to bathe.

sanskrit: tāṃ dadarśa mahātejā menakāṃ kuśikātmajaḥ rūpeṇāpratimāṃ tatra vidyutaṃ jalade yathā
english: The son of Kuśika of great splendour beheld Menakā there — unrivalled in beauty, like lightning amid a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā kandarpavaśago munis tām idam abravīt apsaraḥ svāgataṃ te 'stu vasa ceha mamāśrame anugṛhṇīṣva bhadraṃ te madanena sumohitam
english: Seeing her, the sage, fallen under the power of Kandarpa (Kāma), spoke to her: 'Welcome to you, O apsaras; dwell here in my hermitage and bless me — good fortune to you — who am utterly bewildered by Madana.'

sanskrit: ity uktā sā varārohā tatrāvāsam athākarot tapaso hi mahāvighno viśvāmitram upāgataḥ
english: Thus addressed, that lady of noble hips made her abode there — for a great obstacle to austerity had come upon Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vasantyāṃ varṣāṇi pañca pañca ca rāghava viśvāmitrāśrame saumya sukhena vyaticakramuḥ
english: While she was dwelling there, O Rāghava, O gentle one, ten years (five and five) passed happily in Viśvāmitra's hermitage.

sanskrit: atha kāle gate tasmin viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ savrīḍa iva saṃvṛttaś cintāśokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Then, when that time had passed, the great sage Viśvāmitra became as if filled with shame, overcome with anxiety and grief.

sanskrit: buddhir muneḥ samutpannā sāmarṣā raghunandana sarvaṃ surāṇāṃ karmaitat tapo'paharaṇaṃ mahat
english: The thought arose in the sage's mind, indignant, O joy of the Raghu line: 'All this is the work of the gods — this great plundering of my austerity.'

sanskrit: ahorātrāpadeśena gatāḥ saṃvatsarā daśa kāmamohābhibhūtasya vighno 'yaṃ pratyupasthitaḥ
english: Under the guise of days and nights, ten years have passed; overwhelmed by the delusion of desire, this obstacle has befallen me.

sanskrit: viniḥśvasan munivaraḥ paścāttāpena duḥkhitaḥ
english: Heaving a deep sigh, that best of sages, afflicted with remorse.

sanskrit: bhītām apsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā vepantīṃ prāñjaliṃ sthitām menakāṃ madhurair vākyair visṛjya kuśikātmajaḥ uttaraṃ parvataṃ rāma viśvāmitro jagāma ha
english: Seeing the apsaras Menakā standing frightened and trembling with joined palms, the son of Kuśika dismissed her with gentle words and, O Rāma, Viśvāmitra departed to the northern mountain.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhiṃ jetukāmo mahāyaśāḥ kauśikītīram āsādya tapas tepe sudāruṇam
english: Having resolved upon unswerving resolve and desiring to conquer himself, that greatly renowned sage went to the bank of the river Kauśikī and practised most severe austerity.

sanskrit: tasya varṣasahasraṃ tu ghoraṃ tapa upāsataḥ uttare parvate rāma devatānām abhūd bhayam
english: As he practised that terrible austerity for a thousand years on the northern mountain, O Rāma, fear arose among the gods.

sanskrit: amantrayan samāgamya sarve sarṣigaṇāḥ surāḥ maharṣiśabdaṃ labhatāṃ sādhv ayaṃ kuśikātmajaḥ
english: All the gods, assembled together along with the host of sages, took counsel: 'Let this son of Kuśika rightly obtain the title of maharṣi.'

sanskrit: devatānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ abravīn madhuraṃ vākyaṃ viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam
english: Hearing the words of the gods, the Pitāmaha of all worlds spoke sweet words to Viśvāmitra, that treasury of austerity.

sanskrit: maharṣe svāgataṃ vatsa tapasogreṇa toṣitaḥ mahattvam ṛṣimukhyatvaṃ dadāmi tava kauśika
english: O Maharṣi, welcome, my child — I am pleased by your severe austerity; I grant you greatness and the foremost rank among the sages, O Kauśika.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ sa vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitras tapodhanaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā pratyuvāca pitāmaham
english: Hearing those words of Brahmā, Viśvāmitra the treasury of austerity, bowing with joined palms, replied to the Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: brahmarṣi śabdam atulaṃ svārjitaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ yadi me bhagavān āha tato 'haṃ vijitendriyaḥ
english: If the Blessed One says that I have earned by my own meritorious deeds the incomparable title of brahmarṣi, then I am one who has conquered the senses.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato brahmā na tāvat tvaṃ jitendriyaḥ yatasva muniśārdūla ity uktvā tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: Then Brahmā said to him: 'You have not yet conquered the senses; strive on, O tiger among sages,' — and having said so, departed to the three heavens.

sanskrit: viprasthiteṣu deveṣu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ ūrdhvabāhur nirālambo vāyubhakṣas tapaś caran
english: When the gods had departed, the great sage Viśvāmitra continued his austerity with arms raised, without support, subsisting on air alone.

sanskrit: dharme pañcatapā bhūtvā varṣāsv ākāśasaṃśrayaḥ śiśire salilasthāyī rātryahāni tapodhanaḥ
english: Abiding in righteousness, he subjected himself to the five fires (pañcatapa) in summer; in the rains he sheltered under the open sky; in winter he stood in water — day and night, that treasury of austerity.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi tapo ghoram upāgamat
english: Thus he pursued terrible austerity for a thousand years.

sanskrit: tasmin saṃtapyamāne tu viśvāmitre mahāmunau saṃbhramaḥ sumahān āsīt surāṇāṃ vāsavasya ca
english: While that great sage Viśvāmitra was burning in austerity, great alarm arose among the gods and Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: rambhām apsarasaṃ śakraḥ saha sarvair marudgaṇaiḥ uvācātmahitaṃ vākyam ahitaṃ kauśikasya ca
english: Śakra (Indra), together with all the hosts of Maruts, spoke to the apsaras Rambhā words that were beneficial to himself and harmful to Kauśika.

sanskrit: surakāryam idaṃ rambhe kartavyaṃ sumahat tvayā lobhanaṃ kauśikasyeha kāmamohasamanvitam
english: O Rambhā, this great service to the gods must be performed by you — the alluring of Kauśika here, accompanied by the delusion of desire.

sanskrit: tathoktā sāpsarā rāma sahasrākṣeṇa dhīmatā vrīḍitā prāñjalir bhūtvā pratyuvāca sureśvaram
english: Thus addressed, O Rāma, that apsaras, by the wise Sahasrākṣa, stood ashamed with joined palms and replied to the lord of gods.

sanskrit: ayaṃ surapate ghoro viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ krodham utsrakṣyate ghoraṃ mayi deva na saṃśayaḥ tato hi me bhayaṃ deva prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: O lord of gods, this terrible great sage Viśvāmitra will surely release terrible wrath upon me, O god — there is no doubt. That is why I am afraid, O god; you ought to show your grace to me.

sanskrit: tām uvāca sahasrākṣo vepamānāṃ kṛtāñjalim mā bhaiṣi rambhe bhadraṃ te kuruṣva mama śāsanam
english: Sahasrākṣa spoke to her as she trembled with joined palms: 'Fear not, O Rambhā — good fortune to you; carry out my command.'

sanskrit: kokilo hṛdayagrāhī mādhave ruciradrume ahaṃ kandarpasahitaḥ sthāsyāmi tava pārśvataḥ
english: A cuckoo, captivating the heart, will be perched in a lovely tree in the spring season — I myself, together with Kandarpa (Kāma), will stand at your side.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi rūpaṃ bahuguṇaṃ kṛtvā paramabhāsvaram tam ṛṣiṃ kauśikaṃ rambhe bhedayasva tapasvinam
english: You must assume a form of manifold excellence and supreme radiance, O Rambhā, and break the resolve of that ascetic sage Kauśika.

sanskrit: sā śrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtvā rūpam anuttamam lobhayām āsa lalitā viśvāmitraṃ śucismitā
english: She, having heard his words, assumed an incomparable form and, graceful and bright-smiled, began to allure Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: kokilasya tu śuśrāva valgu vyāharataḥ svanam saṃprahṛṣṭena manasā tata enām udaikṣata
english: He heard the sweet sound of the cuckoo singing, and with a gladdened mind he then looked upon her.

sanskrit: atha tasya ca śabdena gītenāpratimena ca darśanena ca rambhāyā muniḥ saṃdeham āgataḥ
english: Then, from that sound, the incomparable song, and the sight of Rambhā, the sage became filled with suspicion.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣasya tat karma vijñāya munipuṃgavaḥ rambhāṃ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ śaśāpa kuśikātmajaḥ
english: Recognising that deed as the work of Sahasrākṣa, the son of Kuśika, that bull among sages, possessed by rage, cursed Rambhā.

sanskrit: yan māṃ lobhayase rambhe kāmakrodhajayaiṣiṇam daśavarṣasahasrāṇi śailī sthāsyasi durbhage
english: Because you, O Rambhā, seek to allure me who strive to conquer desire and anger, you shall stand as a stone for ten thousand years, O wretched one.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ sumahātejās tapobalasamanvitaḥ uddhariṣyati rambhe tvāṃ matkrodhakaluṣīkṛtām
english: A brāhmaṇa of great splendour, endowed with the power of austerity, shall release you, O Rambhā, who have been polluted by my wrath.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ aśaknuvan dhārayituṃ kopaṃ saṃtāpam āgataḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the great sage Viśvāmitra of great splendour, unable to restrain his anger, was overcome with anguish.

sanskrit: tasya śāpena mahatā rambhā śailī tadābhavat vacaḥ śrutvā ca kandarpo maharṣeḥ sa ca nirgataḥ
english: By his great curse, Rambhā became a stone at that moment; and Kandarpa, having heard the words of the great sage, also departed.

sanskrit: kopena sa mahātejās tapo 'paharaṇe kṛte indriyair ajitai rāma na lebhe śāntim ātmanaḥ
english: That one of great splendour, his austerity having been carried off by unmastered senses, O Rāma, found no peace within himself on account of his anger.
